title: AI for Pancreatic Cancer Imaging
abstract: Developing deep-learning methods for pancreatic cancer analysis from CT imaging, including multi-structure segmentation, tumor detection, anomaly detection, uncertainty estimation, and synthetic medical imaging. Current work investigates pancreas, tumor, duct, vascular, and surrounding anatomical structures to support computer-assisted diagnosis and quantitative analysis.
collaborators: Mayo Clinic - Department of Gastroenterology and Hepatology
Wes Parker — University of California, San Diego (UCSD)
Harsha Pillaresetti — University of California, Santa Barbara (UCSB)

title: Cancer Genomics and Multi-Omics
abstract: Developing machine-learning approaches for pancreatic cancer characterization using DNA methylation, gene-expression, and single-cell data. Current work investigates class imbalance, feature selection, cancer-associated genes, pathway enrichment, and integration of molecular data for improved disease characterization.
collaborators: Masonic Cancer Center, University of Minnesota

title: IVC Filter Detection and Complication Assessment
abstract: Deep-learning and medical-image-analysis methods for detecting and segmenting inferior vena cava filters in CT imaging and supporting automated assessment of filter-related complications.
collaborators: Mayo Clinic Health System — Interventional Radiology

title: NurseAI: AI-Driven Immersive Nursing Simulation
abstract: Developing a multi-agent, AI-driven simulation environment for nursing education. The system uses locally hosted language models to simulate patients, family members, and clinical personnel, enabling adaptive communication scenarios and automated assessment of clinical communication, de-escalation, and decision-making.
collaborators: University of Wisconsin–Eau Claire College of Nursing

title: CABG Outcomes and Clinical Decision Support
abstract: Retrospective analysis of CABG outcomes using ML for risk stratification and protocol optimization across institutional cohorts.
collaborators: Mayo Clinic Health System - Cardiac Surgery

title: Generative AI and Clinical Decision Support
abstract: Developing retrieval-augmented generation and generative AI systems for healthcare applications, including patient education, clinical information retrieval, and AI-assisted health coaching. Current work investigates methods for grounding language-model responses in curated medical knowledge while supporting privacy-aware and locally deployable AI systems.

title: GeoFarmAI: AI for Precision Agriculture
label: Interdisciplinary Collaboration
project_lead: Papia Rozario — University of Wisconsin–Eau Claire
abstract: An interdisciplinary precision-agriculture project led by Papia Rozario at UW–Eau Claire. The Gomes Computational Lab contributes AI, machine-learning, geospatial computing, software development, and student mentorship to the project.
